Charter perks

i

Every time you renew the charter you earn charter points. Spend them here on small, permanent perks that carry into every later charter. Each perk is bought once, deeper perks in a branch need the one before it, and the cost rises with each tier. They are modest tweaks, not stacking multipliers.

Career log

    Fleet Captains

    i

    A ship that becomes a veteran hauler (five round trips on one route) earns a captain's seat for the rest of the charter. You choose which of the four captains to post there. Every captain has a perk and a trade-off, serves on one ship at a time, and can be moved to a different ship once per charter. Nothing is random.

    Loading...

    Loading...

    Working title. Four ships to start (two more purchasable), five colonies, two need-cycles — a lot more to keep an eye on by hand.

    Aurum mines Ore, Verdant grows Grain, Ferrum casts Machinery — the original triangle. Cryo pumps Water and Helion generates Energy, and each needs exactly what the other makes. Ten possible routes, four ships to start, all decided by you.

    Trade Guild

    i

    Now and then the guild offers a bulk contract: deliver a number of units of a good to a colony that needs it before a deadline. You still sell the goods as normal — the contract is an extra bonus. Declining, ignoring or missing one costs nothing.

    Research

    i

    Research points build up on their own over time, separately from your trading profit — they're a second currency spent only on these permanent, fleet-wide upgrades, not on ships or routes.

    Research points: 0

    Research nodes (12)
    Automation Expansion — +1 automation slot
    Fast Ships I — -1 tick travel time, fleet-wide
    Hauler-Class Refit — +50% cargo capacity, fleet-wide
    Galaxy Expansion — Unlocks the Kepler Cluster
    Automation Expansion II — +1 more automation slot (requires Automation Expansion)
    Outer Reaches — Unlocks the Rift Colonies (requires Galaxy Expansion)
    Deep Survey — Long-baseline survey arrays — no direct bonus, but the required first step toward the Umbral Deep (requires Outer Reaches)
    Umbral Reach — Unlocks the Umbral Deep — 3 new colonies, a new need-triangle (requires Deep Survey)
    Autopilot Optimisation (Automation path) — Automated ships earn +10% on every sale
    Autopilot Optimisation II (Automation path) — +1 more automation slot
    Market Insight (Market path) — Sold-down prices recover 50% faster
    Market Insight II (Market path) — Each unit sold pushes its price down 30% less

    Fleet Lab

    i

    Optional extras for your fleet. Nothing here is required to finish the game and nothing here can be lost for good.

    Blueprint Lab

    Design your own hull: spend 9 points on hold, speed and efficiency, name it, save it, and pick it when you buy ship 5 or 6. No design beats every trade-off.

    Trade Crises

    Three handcrafted starting boards with a clear goal and par times for gold, silver and bronze. Your real corporation is set aside and comes back unchanged; nothing in a crisis can be lost, there is no timer to beat and no fail state. Press R to restart the crisis you are playing.

    Hub & Spoke

    Pick one colony as your Distribution Hub: trips between it and its neighbours in the same system take half as long, but its own good holds less in the stockpile. Fleet Priority takes the hub into account.

    Expeditions

    Send one idle, hand-flown ship far from the routes. It cannot trade while it is away; it comes back with a reward and a count on your record.

    Curio cabinet

      Chain Builder

      i

      A puzzle mode apart from your economy: plan a chain of sites that turns a raw good into what a port wants, and spend as few ships as you can. Nothing here is timed, nothing can be lost, and your real corporation is set aside and comes back unchanged.

      24 short puzzles in four chapters. Pick a site for each step of a chain (from the lists, or by clicking the map), put ships on each leg, and lock it in. Your score is the units delivered per ship; par is the best that any chain can do.

      Market prices

      i

      Selling a good repeatedly crashes its price — each unit sold nudges that good's price down, and it only recovers gradually on its own if you leave it alone for a while. Spreading sales across goods keeps prices higher than dumping everything on one.

      Run seed

      Run seed:

      i

      Blackout is an optional harder way to play. The map goes dark, the sparklines are hidden and prices show only as ranges until you buy the information back (a price feed and a star chart, or the research that gives them: Market Insight and Galaxy Expansion). The economy itself does not change. Switch it on before your first sale and keep it on to the endgame for a Dark Run stamp. It is never required for anything.

      Colonies

      i

      A colony's output scales with how well its need is being met, from 0.5x up to 1.5x — an under-supplied colony produces less to trade. Keep delivering enough of what it needs and it develops to Level 2, gaining a second need that reaches into the other supply cycle.

      Fleet priority

      i

      Only affects automated ships that are idle and empty. When on, they'll abandon their fixed shuttle route and reposition themselves toward whichever producer feeds the fleet's most under-served colony, instead of always reloading the same local good.
